7.t: The age of the whole truth; healed of a cold
7.s: The practitioner calls this the age of Christian Science; Thomas studies it and is healed of a cold overnight.
7.q: So I went to this practitioner, and one of the first things he told me, he said, "My boy, we are living in the greatest age that Man ever lived in. We are living in the age of the whole truth." Then he went on to elaborate it: "We are living in the age of Christian Science." That's the way he (?)…

7.t: Lionel Hampton as a Christian Scientist
7.s: Thomas says Hampton is a Christian Scientist reportedly healed of drinking, who showed him how to do the lessons.
7.q: Because I finally met the practitioner that's supposed to have healed him of drinking. I think he was a good student. I don't know whether he went and had his class or not.

535.t: Reincarnation, past lives and a psychic's prediction
535.s: He discusses souls and past lifetimes, recalls studying stars in Peru, and a psychic who predicted a canceled trip when Brubeck's son fell ill.
535.q: Yeah. The way you said the sentence is, to me, what soul passed to me. It’s like my soul, which they say souls are eternal and they say that they have hundreds of lifetimes. And you have to experience, this is the great teachers talking about reincarnation. You have to be a saint and you have to be…

407.t: Converting to Islam and views on God
407.s: He explains his conversion through belief in the oneness of God, contrasting Christianity and Judaism.
407.q: What it is, it was the idea, the clarity of the oneness of God you know. To me God is singular you know. And I had no partners, and Christianity — well Judaism is that way. They, you know, it’s just God that’s it. But Christianity got three Gods. Now they say it’s one God but in three parts you…

395.t: State of the country, faith, River of Life and Thomas Dorsey
395.s: Max Roach's remark, his Christian faith, the meaning of River of Life and Dorsey's Precious Lord story.
395.q: Oh well it’s like Max Roach he told me he said I can’t save the world. I mean he’s lived such a full life and you kind of see the roller coaster and the changing trends. I don’t know you know part of it is I guess being a Christian you have faith. And sometimes, well I guess the recording that…

608.t: Spirituality in his playing; first hearing Charice
608.s: Spirituality comes out in his saxophone; he describes weeping on hearing singer Charice.
608.q: Oh yeah. Um hum. I can’t brag but when people heard me when I was younger, some people were touched, other people like Leonard Feather said I sounded like a wet noodle one day, so it could have hurt my feelings. But like when I play “Over the Rainbow” for example, a lot of times people cry. I’ve…

944.s: He belongs to no religion but credits God for his ability and tries to be a good person.
944.q: I don’t know. I have faith in what I believe in you know. I don’t understand a lot of things and so I don’t join any religions or anything like that. Because I don’t understand it. And what I do understand is most religions don’t make sense to me you know. So all I know is what I call God and what…

551.t: Spirit, mortal mind and giving up smoking
551.s: Williams speaks of the Great Spirit and Christian Science's immortal mind; talk drifts to smoking.
551.q: And you always deal with the spirit of those that loved you. Like part Indian and part African. Okay. O Great Spirit, yes, the Great Spirit that you know is part of all of us. Some people say there’s more to mortal mind. I wonder about that sometimes.

651.t: Spirituality, church and wanting to help people
651.s: Methodist church for 68 years, now Unity, interest in life and death, and his wish to help others globally.
651.q: We probably have, but I can’t think of what they all are. But one thing does come to mind. I started going to a Methodist church, a neighbor took me and my two brothers, when I was about 5 years old. So I’ve always kind of been interested in religion, always gone every Sunday, to Sunday School and…

589.t: Religion as something you do on Sunday
589.s: Lewis says religion is culture-bound and many people leave it behind on Monday, while religious leaders stay silent.
589.q: I think – as I mentioned earlier, I come from a very religious family. Religion was very important to us. I’m sure my parents in their own way were very spiritual. I didn’t learn about spirituality or the Spirit. You hear about the Holy Spirit, but that’s over there or up there or in the book. But…

492.s: He explains following Vedanta, the harmony of religions and his universal outlook, and mentions the Monterey award.
492.q: And keep getting that lesson. The reason I'm here was that I was following the path of Vedanta. I was studying all the world religions and I came across Vedanta. Vedanta teaches the harmony of all religions, Islam school, they got a temple right down the road there, they got Buddhism, they got a…

953.t: His purpose in life, and the mortar prayer as a boy
953.s: He says his purpose is to be a better person and recalls praying when a piece of mortar he dropped nearly hit a man.
953.q: Um, my purpose, I think, is to make myself a better person. That’s the only purpose I can have. And what is a better person? Well, again, that’s between Larry and you, and my friend and him. I don’t, I don’t what a better person is to everybody–

452.t: How a newspaper prayer turned him around in the hospital
452.s: Bitter in the hospital, Cobb cut out the daily prayer from the Daily News and memorized it; it changed his life and remains his strength.
452.q: Right. All right now to get to the prayer that we talked about how I came about this prayer, is this. I'm in the hospital for the second time, and I'm bitter now.

233.s: Monk talks about being a religious person who believes things happen by fate, as with Red Norvo.
233.ch: Wes's death and Monk's turning point
233.q: : That was even stranger. I've got such a...My life went into all kinds of directions after that was fulfilling, very fulfilling. And so many things happened because of... Well, some people would say they were freak things happening. I don't like that word 'freak'; I like the word fate.

386.s: He returns to his belief that Jerusalem and Bethlehem were in heaven as an example of unseen realities.
386.ch: New York, Philadelphia and Harlem nightlife
386.q: Same thing. So many of the things with which we are confronted in life are not real. They are real, but we don't see them as being real. Can you imagine me thinking 'til I was thirty that "walking Jerusalem." I thought I had to be in heaven. I thought when he said, "Go to Jerusalem" he meant that,…
